title: legal redlines scratchpad - ryan murphy
content:
Notes to self / negotiation points for customer contract (Dedicated/Private deployments)

High-level buckets to watch:
- Indemnity (broad vs. narrow; third-party claims re: IP/DMCA; data-related claims)
- Liability cap & exclusions (cap = fees paid in last 12 months? 24 months?; carve outs for gross negligence/fraud)
- Data use & ownership (customer data, prompts, outputs, telemetry)
- Security & compliance (SOC2, pen test, breach notification SLA, KMS/BYOK)
- SLA, remedies & termination rights (credits vs. right to terminate; cure periods)
- Confidentiality & permitted disclosures (narrow definition of "Confidential Information")
- Subprocessors & subcontracting (notice, list, right to object in regulated industries)
- Export controls & sanctions clauses
- Transition assistance & data return/destruction
- IP (who owns model outputs? ownership of derivative models? no training on customer data)

Detailed redline thoughts / talking points:
1) Data use / model training:
   - Reject any language that allows provider to use customer data to train or improve models without explicit opt-in.
   - If the counterparty insists on telemetry/usage data collection for service improvement, require:
       * explicit limited purpose (ops/monitoring/bugfixing) and no training for model weights
       * data to be aggregated/anonymized + documented examples of fields retained
       * ability for customer to opt-out or request deletion of logs tied to a specific tenant
       * BYOK / KMS option for Private deployments; encryption at rest + in transit mandatory
   - Proposed clause: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data to train or improve any machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent." (keep strong)

2) IP / outputs:
   - Be careful around "outputs" language. Customer should own or have an irrevocable license to outputs produced from their inputs.
   - Push back on any language granting provider ownership in derivative works built from customer prompts/outputs.
   - If provider wants rights to aggregated anonymized outputs for benchmarking, limit to non-identifying aggregates and require prior notice.

3) Liability cap / exclusions:
   - Aim cap = fees paid in prior 12 months. If customer commercial size justifies, negotiate to 24 months.
   - Keep consequential damages excluded, but carve out for breaches of confidentiality, willful misconduct, gross negligence.
   - Ensure "gross negligence" is defined/narrowed. Watch for open-ended carve-outs that swallow the cap.

4) Indemnity:
   - Mutual IP indemnity is ideal (we defend our customers against provider IP claims and vice versa) but vendor will likely push for provider indemnifying customer for IP infringement.
   - Push to limit provider's indemnity to claims arising from provider-delivered software/models (not customer prompts or data).

5) Security & breach response:
   - Require 72-hour initial notification for breaches affecting Customer Data (industry sometimes 48h; ask for 72 if vendor pushes back).
   - Require periodic pen test results or attestation (SOC2 Type II report annually).
   - Require cooperation on DSARs if vendor processes personal data; specify timing/costs for support.

6) Audit rights & compliance:
   - Narrow on-sight audit frequency and scope. Prefer quarterly remote attestations + annual on-site with reasonable notice (30 days).
   - If vendor resists full audit, accept independent auditor reports (SOC2) and right to reasonable additional checks for high-risk customers.

7) SLA & Remedies:
   - Prefer credits over termination for SLA misses. Termination for repeated SLA misses only after defined cure periods and escalation (30 days to cure after 2 consecutive months of SLA < X).
   - Define clear metrics (p50/p90 latency, availability % per region, request success rate) and measurement methodology.

8) Termination & transition:
   - Transition assistance for 90 days minimum with defined scope (data export formats, staff support).
   - Require secure data deletion certification within 30 days of termination unless legal hold applies.

9) Subprocessors & cross-border transfer:
   - Need explicit list + 30 days notice for new subprocessors.
   - For EU customers, ensure SCCs and adequate safeguards for transfers.

10) Confidentiality:
   - Narrow the definition of Confidential Information to exclude "general knowledge" and aggregated anonymized data.
   - Ensure reverse engineers clause not used to claim outputs/confidentiality over customer's prompts.

Redline examples / concrete edit suggestions (phrasing suggestions):
- Replace: "Company may use Customer Data to improve models"
  With: "Company may use Customer Data for operational purposes (support, debugging) but shall not use Customer Data to train, tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent."
  
- Replace broad audit: "Customer may audit Company at any time"
  With: "Customer may request an audit once per calendar year, subject to 30 days' prior written notice; Company may satisfy this obligation by providing a current SOC2 Type II report and reasonable written responses to specific questions."

Open / unresolved items to follow up on:
- Pricing/termination interplay — if customer terminates for convenience, do we get pro-rata refund? Need to flag to finance (JIRA: FIN-312).
- Export control clause vague — clarify with export compliance team whether any model or data localization requirements apply (ENG-1234).
- Insurance requirements — vendor asking for $10M; propose $5M with tailored endorsements for cyber (LEGAL-4567).
- Metrics: confirm what Redwood's standard measurement windows are for p90 latency (ops asked: OPS-88).

Work plan / next steps:
- Share draft redlines with solutions-eng for technical feasibility (Ava).
- Run counterparty redline through playbook to auto-apply standard positions (use CONFLUENCE-REDLINES-7890 templates).
- Schedule call with vendor legal to confirm training/data usage language; have fallback wording ready (mutual non-training + telemetry opt-in).

Quick negotiation checklist (one-liners to use on call):
- "We cannot permit training on customer data without explicit opt-in and MD5 hashed opt-out mechanism."
- "Liability cap = fees paid in prior 12 months; carve-outs only for willful misconduct/fraud."
- "We need SOC2 Type II annually and 72-hr breach notification for customer data."
- "Customer retains ownership of outputs and grants Company a limited license only for operations/analytics in anonymized form."

Notes to self (informal):
- watch for sneaky "for any purpose" phrasing re: "use" — always push to define purpose.
- insist on examples of telemetry fields retained (do they log full prompts?).
- ask eng if logs include raw prompts or truncated/hashes. if raw prompts are stored -> escalate.

References / helpful templates:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REDLINES-7890 (redlines playbook)
- Jira: JIRA-LEGAL-4567 (insurance & indemnity papering)
- Ops ticket: OPS-88 (latency measurement)

Last edit notes: 2026-03-01 10:15 AM — moved liability cap to 12 months default; added explicit BYOK callout for Private deployments.

--- end scratchpad ---
